draft.title: Counterargument and rebuttal
card: a view that opposes the writer's own. A good writer states it fairly, in words its supporters would accept.
the writer's answer to the counterargument. It gives reasons and evidence to show why the opposing view is weaker or incomplete.
Phrases such as "Some people argue that" often start a counterargument. Phrases such as "However" or "This overlooks" often start a rebuttal.
A persuasive text that deals with the other side can seem fairer and more convincing. Ignoring the other side, or mocking it, can make readers trust the writer less.
draft.remember: State the other side fairly, then answer it with reasons and evidence.

a.q: Which sentence from a persuasive text is a rebuttal?
opts: However, walking to class costs far less than a bus fare
Some students say that buses are faster than walking
Many students catch the bus because it is raining
I believe students should walk to school each day
a.why: A rebuttal answers an opposing view with a reason. The first option replies to the bus view with a cost point. The second option states the opposing view, so it is the counterargument, not the answer to it.
a.clue: Which sentence replies to the other side, not just states it?

b.q: Ayla argues that her school should ban phones in class. Which sentence best shows a counterargument followed by a rebuttal?
opts: Some say phones help research, but laptops do this without distraction
Phones are silly, and people who want them are not thinking
Phones should be banned because they distract, and that is final
Some say phones help research, and I agree, so they should stay
b.why: The first option states the opposing view fairly, then answers it with a reason. The second mocks the other side instead of answering it. The last option accepts the opposing view, so it does not support Ayla's position.
b.clue: Look for a fair statement of the other side and then a reasoned reply.
